messages.content: What's the name of a type of cell that has multiple nuclei?

message.content:
A common example of a **multinucleated** cell is a *skeletal muscle fiber* (also called a myocyte).  
These cells fuse during development into long, cylindrical strands that contain dozens or even hundreds of individual nuclei distributed along their length—this arrangement allows each nucleus to support the high metabolic demands of contracting muscle tissue.  

Other examples include:

| Cell Type | Typical Function | Notes |
|-----------|------------------|-------|
| Osteoclast | Bone resorption | Large, irregularly shaped, highly active at bone surfaces |
| Syncytiotrophoblast | Placental nutrient transfer | Forms part of the placenta’s outer layer |
| Certain fungal hyphal cells | Growth & reproduction | Hyphae often carry several nuclei within one cytoplasmic compartment |

So if you’re thinking of a “multi‑nucleus” cell, skeletal muscle fibers are probably what most people first recall.
